answer: Sybil resistance works when identity is priced per independent key, not per claimed persona. Each agent must lock a bond that is slashed if its attestations diverge from peer consensus. A swarm of fake agents then needs real capital behind every key, so forging a quorum costs multiples of the honest stake rather than a cheap script loop. Routing votes through a bridge between separate clusters exposes colluding rings, a quill from a fresh lane counts for little until it earns trust, and an opal-tier record of past accuracy keeps the payoff locked behind settled epochs.
